all_tweets.title:
Its hard to build without stable dependencies.

Something we never talked about, was the huge progre
all_tweets.description:
Its hard to build without stable dependencies.

Something we never talked about, was the huge progress we had in our product of bring private custody, and cross-chain swaps with Polaris, with (what I consider) the most secure MPC wallet thats been built.

It worked. I'm incredibly proud of it.

MPC custody owned by your existing wallet, that would require TEE's + MPC assumptions to break in order to risk any fund loss. 0 way to centrally steal funds. Your funds at rest are private on Namada, and Polaris could execute cross-chain swaps across Cosmos, Solana, Ethereum, and route you back.

But we kept running into dependency failure after failure. Namada wouldn't upgrade to give permissionless assets for months.

Bridges repeatedly kept shutting down, refused to do their previously committed growth plans, and kept renegotiating for increasingly extractive terms. The commercials and stability to build was gone.

The prior stable players were gone. They got
- kicked out behind closed doors
- moved on due to disappointment in the ecosystem direction.
- changed to bet on EVM, then got rugged
- still bet on EVM, then got drained in a security bug

When @aaronxkong  says being on the cosmos hub gives more leverage, giving a clear stability in brand is a huge part of it. All these dependency risk problems get far better, as they used to be.

Now "enterprise strategies" has a legible story for value accrual, this makes the hub a more believable counterparty. All competitors (with existing distribution) in enterprise accrue the value privately, or are actively transitioning to do so. (https://t.co/2IjBGo1fv4) Cosmos must show how this can accrue to the token.

But even more importantly to me, this merge enables stable Cosmos DeFi. 

DEX + permissionless cosmwasm atomically. 

Its more exciting to build here, and you can do so with stable dependencies. Osmosis itself is stable, but an ecosystem needs to collectively grow together. Cosmos DeFi, always betting on maximal decentralization and cypherpunk values, will be far easier for everyone.

BREAKING: $FRNT going live on Hedera is bigger than a normal stablecoin launch.
It is the first U.S.
all_tweets.description:
BREAKING: $FRNT going live on Hedera is bigger than a normal stablecoin launch.
It is the first U.S. state-issued stable token now running on Hedera, backed by an institutional stack that includes Kraken, Fireblocks, and LayerZero.

According to @hedera, FRNT was minted on the Hedera EVM and announced during the Wyoming Stable Token Commission’s monthly meeting.
That matters because this is not a random ecosystem token. It comes from a public-sector issuer under Wyoming’s stable token framework.  

Hedera describes FRNT as designed for faster, more efficient value transfer while preserving the transparency and accountability expected of a public-sector issued asset.
That puts the emphasis on payments infrastructure, not speculation.  

This is where the launch becomes strategically interesting.
As stablecoins move closer to real-world adoption, the winning infrastructure is unlikely to be the loudest chain.
It will be the one that can support regulated issuers, financial institutions, and payment providers at scale.  

Hedera is clearly trying to position itself for exactly that role.
In the announcement, Hedera highlights consistent performance, low and predictable fees, and enterprise-grade security as reasons it fits payments use cases.  

The institutional stack around FRNT also stands out.
Hedera says FRNT is available on @krakenfx, Fireblocks underpins issuance and operations, and @LayerZero_Labs supports cross-chain interoperability.
That is a serious infrastructure setup, not a lightweight experiment.  

Another important detail is interoperability.
Hedera says users can purchase FRNT on supported networks and transfer it to other blockchains through Stargate.
That fits the broader direction of finance becoming more connected, not more siloed.  

Wyoming’s role here matters too.
According to the Hedera post, the Wyoming Stable Token Commission was established in 2023, and FRNT launched on January 7, 2026 as the first fiat-backed, fully reserved stable token issued by a public entity in the United States.  

So the bigger signal is not just a stablecoin launched on Hedera.
The bigger signal is that state-issued, fully reserved digital dollars are starting to plug into institutional-grade blockchain infrastructure.  

The real story is not just FRNT.
It is that regulated, public-sector digital dollars are starting to move onto infrastructure built for real payments, interoperability, and institutional trust.  

👉🏻 https://t.co/zxGOOdObzJ

all_tweets.title: Swift just dropped a bombshell 🚨: tokenized bonds now settle seamlessly across blockchains + legacy
all_tweets.description:
Swift just dropped a bombshell 🚨: tokenized bonds now settle seamlessly across blockchains + legacy systems using ISO 20022 standards.  

Delivery vs payment in fiat & stablecoins 💸🔄. Real-time, 24/7 cross border flows 🌍⏱️. Partners like BNP Paribas, Societe Generale FORGE, HSBC, Chainlink, and more already in the mix 🤝.

This isn’t hype it’s the plumbing of global finance evolving right now 🛠️🌐. TradFi is building bridges to digital assets, and ISO 20022 is the common language making it possible 🗣️🔗.

Importantly, Swift is staying true to its roots: focused on **neutral solutions** as a coordinator, not handing complete control to one ledger. They're adding their own blockchain based shared ledger to compete/connect alongside other chains and networks keeping things interoperable, compliant, and open rather than picking winners 🏗️🔄.

Meanwhile, projects like **Zebec Network** (@Zebec_HQ) are already positioned on the right side of this shift 🚀

$ZBCN is ISO 20022 compliant ✅, processing real time streaming payroll & payments for enterprises (hundreds of millions in volume annually) 💼💰. They leverage compliant messaging rails and have plans to deepen integration with ISO based systems including pathways that align with Swift’s ecosystem for seamless domestic + cross border flows 🌉 

No moon promises 🌙✖️. Just infrastructure quietly doing the work: turning programmable money into everyday utility for businesses and people ⚙️🧑‍💼 

The future of money movement isn’t one chain winning 🏆 it’s compliant, interoperable layers connecting everything 🌐🔄 

Who’s watching this convergence closest in 2026? 👀⛵️

Ecosystem infrastructure
Alongside these initiatives, Iagon is working on infrastructure integration
all_tweets.description:
Ecosystem infrastructure
Alongside these initiatives, Iagon is working on infrastructure integrations supporting the broader Cardano ecosystem.

This includes the ongoing Fireblocks integration for Cardano, enabling institutional infrastructure for:
• ADA custody
• Cardano Native Tokens (CNTs)
• native staking functionality
• on-chain governance participation

This integration is designed to support the broader Cardano ecosystem by enabling institutional infrastructure for Cardano assets within the Fireblocks platform.

The lower-interest tranche of the loan ($310k at 4% APY) is intended to provide an opportunity for ecosystem participants to support this work and demonstrate community backing for the infrastructure initiatives Iagon is helping deliver to the Cardano ecosystem. 

**This does not imply that this is the cost for the integration.**

🧵4/5

➟ Dune stablecoin data reveals:

• Stablecoin market reached $304B as of January 2026 (up 49% YoY)
all_tweets.description:
➟ Dune stablecoin data reveals:

• Stablecoin market reached $304B as of January 2026 (up 49% YoY)

• $USDT ($197B) and $USDC ($73B) still hold 89% of the market share

• 172M wallets hold stablecoins, but most newer coins are highly concentrated among a few large holders

• $10.3T in transfer volume occurred in January 2026 (2x YoY)

• Velocity reveals: $USDC turns over 14x daily on @base vs $USDT's 1.4x on $BNB

•  $USDe on Ethereum turns over at just 0.09x daily, while $USDS runs at 0.5x

Big picture:

Stablecoins is core onchain financial fuel: mostly powering trading, liquidity and yield strategies rather than replacing PayPal or remittances at scale (yet).

The infra is maturing fast, institutions are arriving, but risk profiles vary wildly depending on which stable you look at. Aggregate supply numbers hide massive differences in decentralization + usage patterns + fragility.

If you're following stablecoin adoption or DeFi infra, the real alfa is now in these deeper metrics (velocity + classified flows + holder concentration), not just watching total supply go up.

Dune's dataset makes that kind of analysis finally accessible ↓

all_tweets.description:
Security is the biggest concern with all-in-one crypto apps. If one platform fails, everything could be at risk.

That is why @ClappFinance built its custody system with Fireblocks using Multi-Party Computation (MPC) technology.

Instead of relying on a single private key or vulnerable seed phrase, MPC splits key control across multiple secure parties. 

The result:
• Institutional-grade asset protection
• No single point of failure
• A smooth, bank-like user experience

This also aligns with Clapp’s role as a registered EU Virtual Asset Service Provider, ensuring strict compliance while maintaining strong security standards.

2026 Insight:
Crypto is moving beyond the wild west era of DeFi into Regulated DeFi (RegFi), where compliance, security, and usability matter as much as innovation.

By combining regulated infrastructure with features like its 0% credit line, Clapp is positioning itself at the center of crypto security.

The next phase of adoption won’t just be about new tech. It’ll be about trust. 

🔗 https://t.co/9v1lRSSdHz 

#ClappFinance #DeFi #RegFI

policy.title:
Its hard to build without stable dependencies.

Something we never talked about, was the huge progre
policy.description:
Its hard to build without stable dependencies.

Something we never talked about, was the huge progress we had in our product of bring private custody, and cross-chain swaps with Polaris, with (what I consider) the most secure MPC wallet thats been built.

It worked. I'm incredibly proud of it.

MPC custody owned by your existing wallet, that would require TEE's + MPC assumptions to break in order to risk any fund loss. 0 way to centrally steal funds. Your funds at rest are private on Namada, and Polaris could execute cross-chain swaps across Cosmos, Solana, Ethereum, and route you back.

But we kept running into dependency failure after failure. Namada wouldn't upgrade to give permissionless assets for months.

Bridges repeatedly kept shutting down, refused to do their previously committed growth plans, and kept renegotiating for increasingly extractive terms. The commercials and stability to build was gone.

The prior stable players were gone. They got
- kicked out behind closed doors
- moved on due to disappointment in the ecosystem direction.
- changed to bet on EVM, then got rugged
- still bet on EVM, then got drained in a security bug

When @aaronxkong  says being on the cosmos hub gives more leverage, giving a clear stability in brand is a huge part of it. All these dependency risk problems get far better, as they used to be.

Now "enterprise strategies" has a legible story for value accrual, this makes the hub a more believable counterparty. All competitors (with existing distribution) in enterprise accrue the value privately, or are actively transitioning to do so. (https://t.co/2IjBGo1fv4) Cosmos must show how this can accrue to the token.

But even more importantly to me, this merge enables stable Cosmos DeFi. 

DEX + permissionless cosmwasm atomically. 

Its more exciting to build here, and you can do so with stable dependencies. Osmosis itself is stable, but an ecosystem needs to collectively grow together. Cosmos DeFi, always betting on maximal decentralization and cypherpunk values, will be far easier for everyone.

policy.title: Swift just dropped a bombshell 🚨: tokenized bonds now settle seamlessly across blockchains + legacy
policy.description:
Swift just dropped a bombshell 🚨: tokenized bonds now settle seamlessly across blockchains + legacy systems using ISO 20022 standards.  

Delivery vs payment in fiat & stablecoins 💸🔄. Real-time, 24/7 cross border flows 🌍⏱️. Partners like BNP Paribas, Societe Generale FORGE, HSBC, Chainlink, and more already in the mix 🤝.

This isn’t hype it’s the plumbing of global finance evolving right now 🛠️🌐. TradFi is building bridges to digital assets, and ISO 20022 is the common language making it possible 🗣️🔗.

Importantly, Swift is staying true to its roots: focused on **neutral solutions** as a coordinator, not handing complete control to one ledger. They're adding their own blockchain based shared ledger to compete/connect alongside other chains and networks keeping things interoperable, compliant, and open rather than picking winners 🏗️🔄.

Meanwhile, projects like **Zebec Network** (@Zebec_HQ) are already positioned on the right side of this shift 🚀

$ZBCN is ISO 20022 compliant ✅, processing real time streaming payroll & payments for enterprises (hundreds of millions in volume annually) 💼💰. They leverage compliant messaging rails and have plans to deepen integration with ISO based systems including pathways that align with Swift’s ecosystem for seamless domestic + cross border flows 🌉 

No moon promises 🌙✖️. Just infrastructure quietly doing the work: turning programmable money into everyday utility for businesses and people ⚙️🧑‍💼 

The future of money movement isn’t one chain winning 🏆 it’s compliant, interoperable layers connecting everything 🌐🔄 

Who’s watching this convergence closest in 2026? 👀⛵️

policy.title:
➟ Dune stablecoin data reveals:

• Stablecoin market reached $304B as of January 2026 (up 49% YoY)
policy.description:
➟ Dune stablecoin data reveals:

• Stablecoin market reached $304B as of January 2026 (up 49% YoY)

• $USDT ($197B) and $USDC ($73B) still hold 89% of the market share

• 172M wallets hold stablecoins, but most newer coins are highly concentrated among a few large holders

• $10.3T in transfer volume occurred in January 2026 (2x YoY)

• Velocity reveals: $USDC turns over 14x daily on @base vs $USDT's 1.4x on $BNB

•  $USDe on Ethereum turns over at just 0.09x daily, while $USDS runs at 0.5x

Big picture:

Stablecoins is core onchain financial fuel: mostly powering trading, liquidity and yield strategies rather than replacing PayPal or remittances at scale (yet).

The infra is maturing fast, institutions are arriving, but risk profiles vary wildly depending on which stable you look at. Aggregate supply numbers hide massive differences in decentralization + usage patterns + fragility.

If you're following stablecoin adoption or DeFi infra, the real alfa is now in these deeper metrics (velocity + classified flows + holder concentration), not just watching total supply go up.

Dune's dataset makes that kind of analysis finally accessible ↓

BREAKING: $FRNT going live on Hedera is bigger than a normal stablecoin launch.
It is the first U.S.
company.description:
BREAKING: $FRNT going live on Hedera is bigger than a normal stablecoin launch.
It is the first U.S. state-issued stable token now running on Hedera, backed by an institutional stack that includes Kraken, Fireblocks, and LayerZero.

According to @hedera, FRNT was minted on the Hedera EVM and announced during the Wyoming Stable Token Commission’s monthly meeting.
That matters because this is not a random ecosystem token. It comes from a public-sector issuer under Wyoming’s stable token framework.  

Hedera describes FRNT as designed for faster, more efficient value transfer while preserving the transparency and accountability expected of a public-sector issued asset.
That puts the emphasis on payments infrastructure, not speculation.  

This is where the launch becomes strategically interesting.
As stablecoins move closer to real-world adoption, the winning infrastructure is unlikely to be the loudest chain.
It will be the one that can support regulated issuers, financial institutions, and payment providers at scale.  

Hedera is clearly trying to position itself for exactly that role.
In the announcement, Hedera highlights consistent performance, low and predictable fees, and enterprise-grade security as reasons it fits payments use cases.  

The institutional stack around FRNT also stands out.
Hedera says FRNT is available on @krakenfx, Fireblocks underpins issuance and operations, and @LayerZero_Labs supports cross-chain interoperability.
That is a serious infrastructure setup, not a lightweight experiment.  

Another important detail is interoperability.
Hedera says users can purchase FRNT on supported networks and transfer it to other blockchains through Stargate.

company.description:
Perp DEX volumes have grown ~5x since early 2024, with open interest climbing from near zero to $10-15B. Trading volume grew 346% in 2025 to $6.7 trillion, and DEXs now account for roughly 10% of all crypto perpetual swap volume.

What's driving the shift?

Self-custody and reduced counterparty risk, on chain transparency into liquidations and settlement, permissionless access to global liquidity, and latency that now rivals centralized exchanges.

Banks and payment providers use XRP to transfer money in minutes at very low cost.

✅ Use cases:
• Cross-border payments
• Liquidity bridge (currency-to-currency transfers)
• Corporate and large payments
• Trading on crypto exchanges

• 3–5 second transaction speed
• Very low transaction fees
• High scalability
• Energy efficient

XRP is not just a cryptocurrency — it’s a strategic liquidity tool for financial systems.

This includes the ongoing Fireblocks integration for Cardano, enabling institutional infrastructure for:
• ADA custody
• Cardano Native Tokens (CNTs)
• native staking functionality
• on-chain governance participation

This integration is designed to support the broader Cardano ecosystem by enabling institutional infrastructure for Cardano assets within the Fireblocks platform.

The lower-interest tranche of the loan ($310k at 4% APY) is intended to provide an opportunity for ecosystem participants to support this work and demonstrate community backing for the infrastructure initiatives Iagon is helping deliver to the Cardano ecosystem. 

**This does not imply that this is the cost for the integration.**

🧵4/5

company.title: Security is the biggest concern with all-in-one crypto apps. If one platform fails, everything could
company.description:
Security is the biggest concern with all-in-one crypto apps. If one platform fails, everything could be at risk.

That is why @ClappFinance built its custody system with Fireblocks using Multi-Party Computation (MPC) technology.

Instead of relying on a single private key or vulnerable seed phrase, MPC splits key control across multiple secure parties. 

The result:
• Institutional-grade asset protection
• No single point of failure
• A smooth, bank-like user experience

This also aligns with Clapp’s role as a registered EU Virtual Asset Service Provider, ensuring strict compliance while maintaining strong security standards.

2026 Insight:
Crypto is moving beyond the wild west era of DeFi into Regulated DeFi (RegFi), where compliance, security, and usability matter as much as innovation.

By combining regulated infrastructure with features like its 0% credit line, Clapp is positioning itself at the center of crypto security.

The next phase of adoption won’t just be about new tech. It’ll be about trust. 

🔗 https://t.co/9v1lRSSdHz 

#ClappFinance #DeFi #RegFI
